name: National accounts

subjectOf.text: Recursive agent to agent productivity gains are invisible to national accounts because they involve no monetary transactions, no employment, and no market exchange as traditionally defined, even though the final output may register in GDP statistics.
subjectOf.abstract: But the intermediate productivity gains, the agent-to-agent improvements that made the optimization possible, are invisible to national accounts because they involve no monetary transactions, no employment, and no market exchange as traditionally defined.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Collapse of Scarcity Economics (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6421319
scope_conditions: applies to intermediate agent to agent improvements within the machine layer

subjectOf.text: Existing national accounts are built to measure terminal human consumption and therefore fail to capture intermediate value created in agent-to-agent transaction chains, so the measurement apparatus requires reconstruction.
subjectOf.abstract: Existing national accounts are designed to measure terminal human consumption and do not capture intermediate value created in agent-to-agent transaction chains where no human consumption event occurs at any step prior to the terminal output. The measurement apparatus requires reconstruction.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Computative Economics A Framework for Economic Analysis under Computational Abundance (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6607458
scope_conditions: applies where value is created in agent-to-agent chains with no intervening human consumption event
